idiom_name: Auth.js (NextAuth) providers array; Passport strategies with types; NestJS guards + strategies
implementation_notes: The TypeScript ecosystem provides the seam at framework level: Auth.js takes a providers array (80+ preconfigured OAuth/OIDC providers plus a Credentials provider whose authorize() returns a user or null), Passport strategies are consumed through DefinitelyTyped types, and NestJS binds them to guards (@UseGuards(AuthGuard('jwt'))). For a hand-rolled service, a named interface Authenticator { authenticate(req): Promise<Principal | null> } plus a Map<string, Authenticator> reproduces the seam; TypeScript adds no runtime enforcement, so the discipline is declaring the principal type once and never widening it per mechanism.
pitfalls: null and undefined differ as failure signals in a typed codebase; declare Promise<Principal | null> and treat thrown errors as verifier failures, not invalid credentials.
Types are erased at runtime: a structural interface is satisfied by any matching object, so keep the auth contract small and test the registry wiring.
Passport typings hide the runtime verify-callback contract; the three outcomes (err, false, user) still apply.
Persisting the whole session user in a signed cookie or JWT exposes fields; store an identifier and reload.
